title: Operator overloading
hook: Operators are static methods with extra syntax. Overload them when the type is a value (money, time, Redis key composition), not when you want cute APIs for workers. C# 14 adds user-defined compound assignment.

sections.heading: Rules of the room
sections.prose: User-defined operators are public static methods named operator + and friends. Equality operators should travel with Equals and GetHashCode (module 05) — overloading == without value equality is how Redis DTO bugs happen. Conversion operators (implicit/explicit) are easy to make surprising; prefer named factory methods for auth tokens. Comparison operators should match IComparable. Do not overload true/false or bitwise ops unless you are writing a flags-like value type.

sections.heading: C# 14 compound assignment
sections.prose: Historically += was rewritten as x = x + y, which copies a struct twice and can surprise mutable value types. C# 14 lets you define compound assignment operators so += can mutate in place when that is the type’s contract. Use it on types where in-place update is the point (a running total struct). Skip it on immutable records — with-expressions are the copy story.

snippets.label: Operator + and a C# 14 compound assignment sketch
snippets.explanation: Money stays immutable and returns a new value from +. RunningTotal uses C# 14 user-defined compound assignment to add in place. Check your language version on .NET 10.

sections.heading: What not to overload
sections.prose: Do not give a worker class operator+ because it “adds a message.” Do not use implicit conversions from string to Token — that hides allocation and parsing failures. Extension members in C# 14 can declare operators on types you do not own; that lives in module 10 with the rest of extension syntax. Finalizers remain unrelated and still belong in module 14.

interviewTakeaways: Operators are static methods; keep them on value-like types.
C# 14 compound assignment can avoid the x = x + y copy.
Pair == with Equals/GetHashCode; details in module 05.
commonPitfalls: Overloading == on a class and forgetting GetHashCode.
Implicit conversions that throw or allocate in surprising places.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS does not let you overload + for a class in a first-class way beyond valueOf hacks. C# operators are real metadata methods.
TS cannot add operators to types. You write add(a, b) functions. C# can make + a named static method.
